_comment: The manifest every harness iterates (never hard-code case names). Reader contract: (1) load every entry of caseFiles and iterate its cases in order; (2) a case bearing excluded[<your engine>] is SKIPPED AS DATA — visit it, log the §9 reason, count it consumed; the excluded keys are exactly the lowercase names in 'engines'; (3) a case bearing expect_fail MUST be reported as failing — a harness that passes it proves nothing; (4) a 'kind' outside 'kinds' is a FAILURE, not a skip; (5) after the run, assert exactly case_count cases were consumed. 'comparisons' defines every comparison value this package uses. GENERATED by src/__tests__/runtime/character-contract-fixtures.test.ts (inputs: the real JSON export; expectations: the HTML runtime) — do not hand-edit; regenerate with REGEN_FIXTURES=1 and re-copy into the three plugin repos.
package: characters-engine-contract §5 golden package, plus the localization §9 arm

kindDefinitions.read: one resolved character value, driven through BOTH runtime surfaces (the char-var node arm and the character API), which must agree. The ref carries a DECOY path naming the other character, so only id-first resolution passes.
kindDefinitions.speaker: a dialogue speaker resolved by characterRefId: the record key the id bridges to, plus that record display name and image. The `character` path field names the OTHER character as the decoy.
kindDefinitions.write: a write through one surface, read back through every surface listed in `reads`. Replay these cases IN ORDER against ONE continuously-held store — they build on each other, which is the one-state property they exist to prove.
kindDefinitions.sweep: the full resolution table after every write case has been replayed in order: every arm on both characters, as the store then stands.
kindDefinitions.save: a save taken after the writes. Character state appears ONLY in the character section (structural, since each engine keeps its own pre-P4 save shape) and the V2 dataAssets key carries no character entries.
kindDefinitions.degraded: one rung of the degraded ladder against its OWN freshly-seeded store. `seedMutation` says how to doctor the loaded state first; `get` says what the miss must answer and `set` whether the write lands.
kindDefinitions.localized: one (language, stringId) expectation: the exact text an engine must produce for that id in that language.
kindDefinitions.language-table: the COMPLETE resolved table for one language — every id the export shipped, so an implementation cannot pass by covering only the named cases.
kindDefinitions.source-only: the absent-sidecar expectation: what every shipped id resolves to when no localization.json is present at all.

comparisons.vendor-verbatim: inputs only: vendor these bytes unchanged into the engine repo — a real export, not an approximation. The harness never compares them against anything; it LOADS them.
comparisons.byte: the expected leaf is an exact string lifted from the input artifacts (string-table key, asset id, record key): compare byte-for-byte.
comparisons.structural: JSON value equality. Array order is significant; map values compare as ORDERED {key, value} entry lists; numbers compare by exact representation equality — every number in this package is binary-exact (a dyadic rational, enforced by a generator assertion), so no tolerance exists anywhere.

statuses.translated: a store entry whose snapshot still matches the source: the translation ships.
statuses.outdated: a store entry stamped against an OLDER source text: the OLD translation ships (user ruling 2), never the new source.
statuses.untranslated: no store entry: the source text ships, so the table is never sparse.
statuses.empty: a store entry whose text is '': treated exactly as untranslated — the source ships and an empty string never overlays anything.

localization.resolution: strings[<language>][<stringId>] -> the keying artifact's own strings.en -> the raw stored value. Never undefined; engines compute NO status, NO hash and NO further fallback. The lookup runs on the AUTHORED template, so any variable interpolation happens AFTER it.
localization.absentSidecar: no localization.json in the export = a pre-localization export, source-only. Branch on the FILE EXISTING, never on a key count.
localization.keyedIn: a case field: the artifact whose `strings.en` is that id's SOURCE TIER — the second step of `resolution`, and the table to fall through to when the language table has no row.
localization.reach: a case field: how the id is ARRIVED AT through a character record — read `characterId`'s variable named `variableName` and take the key it stores. FOLLOW IT; never rebuild the id from the character being read. An inherited value's key names `authoringCharacterId`, the DECLARING ANCESTOR, so a rebuilt id is a plausible implementation that passes every non-inherited case and resolves an inherited one to the raw value.
localization.shippedSet: the sidecar's ids are the ids that KEYED an engine artifact. `.sfui` widget and dropdown strings have NO rows here — they never reach a plugin and localize in the HTML lane — so their absence is the contract, not a bug.
localization.charset: ASCII by design. This package pins RESOLUTION, not text encoding.

provenance.reference: the HTML runtime (the contract reference implementation), seeded as the HTML export lane seeds it
provenance.localizationReference: the export lane itself — §7 pre-applies every translation fallback at export, so the localization.json this package vendors IS the reference for the localization arm (the runtime never re-derives those values).
provenance.note: exporterCommit is HEAD at REGEN time — the commit whose exporter and runtime produced every artifact in this package (the package commit lands immediately on top of it).

inputs.role: the character records every engine already loads (localized: values in the string family are string-table keys)
the id bridge: da_ id -> characters.json record key, used verbatim
the engine-lane script with the additive id fields (characterRefId beside `character`, characterId beside characterPath)
the V2 data-asset seed — pinned CHARACTER-FREE (seed disjointness); init the V2 store from it for the save-double-capture case
inputs.producedBy: JsonExportStrategy (build/data-assets.json), plus one _comment line injected by the generator

inputs.role: the translations sidecar: full, PRE-RESOLVED per-language tables. Load it when it exists; its ABSENCE is a pre-localization export and the only branch an engine takes on it
